page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the AMD EPYC 7H12 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under KVM virtualization, this instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It features 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks position the ecs.g6a.xlarge in the lower-to-mid tiers. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng place the instance in the bottom 10%, while Geekbench single-core and Passmark memory scores reach average mid-tier levels. Memory bandwidth and static web serving throughput are relatively weak, falling into the bottom 25% of tested configurations. This performance profile suggests a trade-off where dedicated CPU resources are provided at a cost-efficient tier, but raw computational throughput and memory speeds remain modest.

Given these characteristics, the ecs.g6a.xlarge is suited for light general-purpose workloads. Appropriate use cases include small-scale web serving, basic application hosting, development environments, and lightweight database operations that do not demand high-speed local storage or intensive parallel processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor running at 2.6 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture with KVM virtualization, it offers a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Benchmark results indicate modest performance, with Geekbench single-core and Passmark memory scores reaching average levels, while stress-ng CPU performance and memory bandwidth fall into the lower tiers. With a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, this instance represents a cost-efficient option for workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation without extreme computational demands. It is best suited for light web serving, development environments, and low-intensity application hosting.
